In this deterministic replay, two distinct witness identities bound to the same {predecessor_blob,effect_key} produce one shared effect identity but two distinct attempt identities.

Reusing the same witness identity with the same effect identity reproduces the same attempt identity, so a same-invocation retry can be recognized deterministically without treating a distinct claimant as the same attempt.

inference: For the exact replayed scheme, separating effect identity from attempt identity removes the claimant-identity ambiguity found in the predecessor leaf: {predecessor_blob,effect_key,witness_identity} is sufficient to distinguish two modeled claimants while {predecessor_blob,effect_key} remains a common intended-effect key. This supports deterministic local duplicate-versus-competition classification, but it does not itself provide mutual exclusion, winner selection, fairness, lease semantics, or exactly-once repository effects. Those require an empirical CAS/create-if-absent child and remain unresolved.
